title: Rings and gaps in the disc around Elias 24 revealed by ALMA
question: What are the gap and ring structures in the Elias 24 1.3 mm continuum, and can an embedded migrating, accreting planet in SPH gas/dust simulations reproduce them?

what.value: Disc dust model, stellar properties, dust mass 0.0017 Msun, rc=127 au, p=0.9, flaring index 1.03, geometry i=24, PA=50

evidence.loc: 3.2.1 Models for the disc surface density structure
evidence.quote: where $M_{\mathrm{d}}=0.0017 M_{\odot}$ is the dust disc mass, $r_{\mathrm{c}}=127$ au is a characteristic scaling radius and $p=0.9$ is the gradient parameter.

evidence.loc: 3.1.2 Radiative transfer and synthetic ALMA observations
evidence.quote: an effective fixed temperature of 4250 K (cite: wilking05a)

what.value: SMA 880 um flux used for spectral index

evidence.quote: Comparing the measured total flux with $880\, \mu m$ SMA emission maps, we obtain a spectral index of $\sim 2.27\pm 0.01$

recipe.method: CASA clean after self-calibration; total flux summed over emission above 2 rms
Azimuthal elliptical annulus photometry; fit sum of three Gaussians
key_parameters: annuli width a quarter of linear resolution

recipe.goal: SPH gas/dust simulations with embedded planet
recipe.method: PHANTOM one-fluid dust, 1 mm grains, sink-particle planet free to migrate and accrete; 10^6 particles; snapshot chosen by eye
key_parameters: alpha_AV=0.1 (alpha_SS~0.003); dust-to-gas 0.1; H_in=0.075 au; r 1-180 au
assumptions: vertically isothermal; initial dust-to-gas ratio 0.1 for mm grains

recipe.method: RADMC-3D dust temperature then ray tracing with 10^8 photons; Fourier transform, sample at ALMA uv, image like data with CASA simulator
key_parameters: grain size 0.005 um-1 mm, m=3.5; star R=4.2 Rsun, T=4250 K
assumptions: star only heating source; inclination/PA from observations

evidence.quote: The measured total flux is $368.1 \pm0.9$ mJy
we obtain a spectral index of $\sim 2.27\pm 0.01$
the dark rings are located at $0.47''$ and $0.71''$ while the bright rings have a semi-major axis of $0.58''$ and $0.87''$

answer_key.quantity: Planet mass and location in best model

evidence.quote: At this stage of the simulation, the planet is at 61.7 au from the central star and its mass is $0.7\, \mathrm{M_{\mathrm{J}}}$.
the mean value of the absolute values of the residuals is $\left(5.1\pm 0.4\right)$% of the observed fluxes
The measured total flux of the disc from the simulated model map is $309.2 \pm1.1$ mJy

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channels and continuum spectral window selection for imaging
Self-calibration solution intervals and number of iterations
Dust opacity table details beyond reference to Andrews et al. 2010
SPH initial planet/disc parameter grid explored and selection of best snapshot (fit by eye)
Number of azimuthal/vertical RADMC-3D grid cells and CASA simulator noise settings
missing_for_reproduction: Simulation input files and parameter grid
Selected snapshot and RT setup details
score_reason: Imaging and profile measurement reproducible from archival data; the hydrodynamic modelling is hard to reproduce exactly.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, stated imaging recipe, numeric ring locations and fluxes.
